mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST drops > 5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases over three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and healthy labor market
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strong supply-side response, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 decreases > 1% QoQ and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
